summary: Spotsylvania County, VA 80-foot Aermotor tower built February 1928 on state land; manned to late 1960s; removed circa 2019; land now private.

facts.design: 80-foot Aermotor tower, with the words 'Prevent Forest Fires' inscribed in the concrete at the foot of the stairs
facts.status_note: Removed circa 2019 per both registers; no source describes what remains on the site

access.note: Land is privately held; the register describes no public access

events.note: Built February 1928 through cooperation between the Virginia Forest Service and the Spotsylvania Forest Fire Protective Association
Radio reported recently installed in a Free Lance-Star item dated April 22, 1957, linking the tower to the Forest Service frequency at Charlottesville
Registered April 27, 2017 as US 1191, VA 38; nominated by Kristin Reynolds
Registered March 24, 2020 as US 1932, VA 35; nominated by James Hull

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register calls it the second tower named Chancellor in Spotsylvania County; a 1928 item quoted by Forest Lookouts calls it Virginia's first 80-foot steel lookout tower. These describe different things and both are kept.

notes_for_editor: Both registers agree on build date (Feb 1928), height (80 ft), ownership and removal (circa 2019). Staffing is only 'manned until the late 1960s' (no exact year), so no staffed_last event is recorded. No fires found in the sources read. The inscription photo credited to Krissy Reynolds is on NHLR, but no source says whether the block remains. A 1961 Forest Lookouts newspaper item mentions an 80-foot tower near Shady Grove Church but does not name Chancellor, so it is not used. Two web searches; the Shady Grove church history blog has no tower material.
